Non-Domestic Rating Decision

Page 1 of 3

Appellant: Mr Daniel Carman

Appellant’s Address: 91 Brynymor Road, Swansea SA1 4JG

Appeal number: 685529893990/192NV17/40

The Matter Appealed against: 2017 Rating List

Date of Hearing: Thursday 8th November 2018

Appearances: Mr D Carman (Appellant) & Mr A Morse (for the respondent
Valuation Officer)

Date of Decision:  22nd November 2018

Decision of Tribunal: Appeal allowed in part

Members of the Tribunal: Mr B Al-Khanchi (Chairman), Mrs A Wingrave &
Mrs LM Thomas

Tribunal Clerk: Mr G Harris

Introduction:
1. Mr Carman contended in a proposal to alter an entry in the 2017 Rating
List, received by the Valuation Officer on 16th October 2017 that the
Rateable Value (RV) of 91 Brynymor Road, Swansea was incorrect and
should be reduced from £14,250 to £11,960 with effect from 1st April
2017.
2. This is a summary of the case and is not intended to be an exhaustive
record of the proceedings. However, the parties can be assured that all
the evidence was fully considered by the tribunal when it arrived at its
decision. Consequently, the absence of reference to any statement, or
evidence, should not be construed as being overlooked.

Summary of the Case

3. Mr Carman explained that he operated a small independent laundrette
and was under a lot of pressure. The RV was currently £14,250 and a
huge burden being 10% of his turnover and 75% of the rent. The RV was
the highest on Brynymor Road. Mr Morse had offered a reduction to
£12,000 but Mr Carman contended that £10,000 would be more in line
with his business costs.
4. Mr Morse explained that the appeal for consideration was a compiled list
appeal relating to the level of value ascribed to the property. He stated

that following an inspection of the property during May 2018 it had been
discovered that the measurements used in the original valuation had been
incorrect; hence he had revised his valuation using the amended survey
and a consideration of impediments due to access and rear stores but
retaining a zone A value of £260/m2. It was for the Tribunal to decide
whether this amount was correct or too high.
5. Referring to a photograph of the appeal property Mr Morse described it as
being located on the middle of Brynymor Road, which comprised mostly
of delicatessens and bars rather than shops and with few empty units. A
plan of the hereditament highlighted the washers and dryers but in effect it
comprised a standard retail space. A map showed its location on
Brynymor Road, with other properties subject to appeals being marked as
settled or outstanding.
6. Mr Morse provided the tribunal with the history of the assessment
together with its rent returns. It was Mr Morse’s opinion that the revised
RV of £12,000 was fair and his valuation was as follows –

7. Mr Morse explained that a schedule of rental evidence showed that rents
varied along Brynymor Road from £190/m2 to an amount in excess of
£300/m2. As such zone A rates of £260 and £240 had been adopted
across Brynymor Road. An appeal at 67 Brynymor Road had been
discussed and agreed at a rate of £240/m2. He confirmed that at £14,250
the appeal property had the highest RV on the street, and that the revised
offer of £12,000 was more in line with the other assessments. Mr Morse
explained that it was up to the tribunal to decide which value to adopt and
that he would have no objections if the Tribunal decided to use £240/m2 in
line with other assessments along the street.
8. At the conclusion of the hearing, the tribunal decided to reserve its
decision.

Non-Domestic Rating Decision

Page 3 of 3
The Reasons for Decision

9. Having considered all the evidence placed before it the tribunal decided
as follows: -

10. In his proposal Mr Carman had contended that the Rating List was
inaccurate and that the RV of the appeal property should be reduced. In
cases such as this higher court authorities had accepted that the burden
of proof rested with the appellant on the basis that ‘he who asserts must
prove’. It was an accepted tenet of law that any assertions made before a
tribunal should be underpinned with evidence. Therefore, in the case
under consideration the persuasive burden of proof rested with the
appellant ratepayer and not the Valuation Officer by virtue of a statutory
duty to prepare and alter the Rating List.
11. In the tribunal’s opinion Mr Carman had not been able to sustain his
contentions that the assessment was incorrect and had not, with
reference to evidence, undermined the Valuation Officer’s valuation of the
property. Looking at all of the available rental evidence submitted by Mr
Morse, together with the agreement made between the parties in respect
of 67 Brynymor Road, the tribunal decided that the zone a value of
£240/m2 used to value part of Brynymor Road should be applied to the
appeal property, noting that Mr Morse had stated that he had no
objections to the use of this amount.

12. Taking into account the tribunals decision that the zone A value of
£240/m2 should be applied to the valuation of the appeal property, the
tribunal’s revised valuation was as follows –
